title: The review check becomes a reusable workflow
summary: The review check's jobs move out of `.github/workflows/review.yml` into a new reusable workflow, `.github/workflows/review-check.yml`, which any repository can call. osf's own `review.yml` shrinks to a single caller job that passes `osf-ref: github.workflow_sha`, so the osf binary is built from the commit of the workflow itself rather than from the pull request's base branch. The build job now checks out that pinned commit into `osf-src` read-only and writes to a separate `build-out`, refuses any `osf-ref` that is not the workflow's own commit, and refuses any event but `pull_request_target`. Fork review moves from the `OSF_REVIEW_FORKS` repository variable to an `allow-forks` input the caller passes. On the osf side, `review reduce` now accepts a folder of saved reviewer files and expands it to the `.json` files inside, and `load_pull_request` accepts a whole code-host event file as well as a bare pull-request object.

lanes.label: Caller
lanes.subtitle: pull_request_target, default branch
lanes.summary: The workflow GitHub reads from the default branch. It holds no step of its own and only names the reusable workflow and the inputs.

lanes.label: Review check
lanes.subtitle: reusable workflow jobs
lanes.summary: The reusable workflow that holds every job: build, one job per reviewer, the deciding job, and the fork-disabled job.

lanes.label: osf binary
lanes.subtitle: Rust CLI, built from the pinned commit
lanes.summary: The osf command line the jobs run. Built once in the build job and handed to every later job as an artifact.

lanes.label: Reviewers and code host
lanes.subtitle: external services
lanes.summary: The model providers each reviewer job reaches, and the GitHub API the deciding job posts through.

nodes.label: review.yml
nodes.subtitle: pull_request_target caller
nodes.summary: osf's own caller. It keeps the `pull_request_target` trigger and the union of the permissions its jobs need, and replaces every job with one `uses:` of the local reusable workflow. It passes `osf-ref: github.workflow_sha` and `osf-repository: github.repository`, so osf comes from the commit of the caller, never from the pull request's base.

nodes.label: review-check.yml
nodes.subtitle: on: workflow_call
nodes.summary: The new reusable workflow. It declares five inputs (`osf-ref`, `osf-repository`, `runs-on`, `verifier-app-id`, `allow-forks`), no `workflow_call` secret, and reads no repository variable. Every job starts with the harden-runner egress block and every action is pinned by full commit SHA.

nodes.label: build job
nodes.subtitle: builds the pinned osf
nodes.summary: Checks out `inputs.osf-ref` from `inputs.osf-repository` into `osf-src` read-only, refuses any ref that is not a full 40-character SHA or that differs from `job.workflow_sha`/`job.workflow_repository`, refuses any event but `pull_request_target`, and builds with `cargo build --release --bin osf` into a separate writable `build-out`. It also runs `osf review work-item` with a read-only token.

nodes.label: reviewer jobs
nodes.subtitle: codex, claude, opencode
nodes.summary: One job per agent in the agent list, each named `review-<agent>`. Each mounts `base` and `pr` read-only, holds only its own provider key from the `review` environment, and runs `osf review run --reviewer <name> --if-enabled`. Each uploads its saved answers as `review-run-<name>` even when it fails.

nodes.label: review job
nodes.subtitle: collects, decides, posts
nodes.summary: The last job. It downloads every `review-run-*` artifact into `out/runs`, mints the verifier app token, and runs `osf review reduce` with the folder as its file argument. It runs even when a reviewer job failed, because a reviewer with no saved answers counts as could-not-run.

nodes.label: review-fork-disabled
nodes.subtitle: fails loudly for forks
nodes.summary: Runs when the head repository is not this repository and `allow-forks` is false. It blocks all egress and exits non-zero, so a fork's pull request cannot pass the check by leaving fork review unconfigured.

nodes.label: osf binary
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf
nodes.summary: The CLI the jobs run. Built once in the build job from the pinned commit and passed to every later job as the `osf-binary` artifact.

nodes.label: osf review reduce
nodes.subtitle: decides and posts
nodes.summary: Reads the saved reviewer files, checks findings against the pull request's files, journals, and posts. It now expands a folder argument to the `.json` files directly inside it, sorted by name, so a workflow can pass the folder it downloaded.

nodes.label: expand_saved_runs
nodes.subtitle: folder to file list
nodes.summary: Turns each path into itself when it is a file, or into the `.json` files directly inside it, sorted by name, when it is a folder. Non-JSON entries and subfolders are skipped.

nodes.label: load_pull_request
nodes.subtitle: event file or bare object
nodes.summary: Parses the pull request's number, title and body. It now unwraps a `pull_request` key first, so a whole code-host event file such as the one `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` names loads as well as a bare object.

nodes.label: review_workflow.rs
nodes.subtitle: checks the workflow text
nodes.summary: Reads both workflow files as text and asserts the shape of the check: the stable input list, no `workflow_call` secret, no repository variable, the pinned-commit guard, the fixed environment names, the single verifier token mint, and that the caller is thin and passes only declared inputs.

nodes.label: review_run.rs
nodes.subtitle: folder argument
nodes.summary: Adds a test that `review reduce` given a folder of saved runs produces the same output as the same files listed explicitly.

nodes.label: development.md
nodes.subtitle: adopter guide
nodes.summary: Documents how another repository calls the review check: the caller shape, the five inputs, why no key is a `workflow_call` secret, what is stable, and the organisation setting a private factory repo needs.

nodes.label: GitHub API
nodes.subtitle: issues, pull requests, checks
nodes.summary: Read by the build job with a read-only token to find the work item, and written by the last job through the verifier app's token to post the review.

nodes.label: Model providers
nodes.subtitle: OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter
nodes.summary: Each reviewer job reaches only its own provider's host, plus the hosts its agent needs to start. The egress allow-list is per job.

edges.label: uses: ./review-check.yml
edges.summary: The caller names the reusable workflow by a local path, which GitHub reads at the same commit as the caller. An adopter names it by a full commit SHA instead.

edges.label: osf-ref = github.workflow_sha
edges.summary: The commit osf is built from is the commit of the workflow itself, not the pull request's base. The build job refuses any other value.

edges.label: cargo build --release
edges.summary: The build job compiles the pinned osf into `build-out` and uploads it as the `osf-binary` artifact.

edges.label: osf review work-item
edges.summary: With a read-only token, the build job finds the issue the pull request names and saves it as the `work-item` artifact.

edges.label: osf review run
edges.summary: Each reviewer job downloads the one binary the build job made and runs it against the read-only `base` and `pr` checkouts.

edges.label: one provider key each
edges.summary: Each reviewer job holds only its own provider's key and reaches only that provider's host.

edges.label: osf review reduce
edges.summary: The last job runs the same binary to collect the saved answers, decide, and post.

edges.label: verifier app token
edges.summary: The last job alone mints the verifier app's token and posts the review and check run.
`review reduce` expands its file arguments before reading them, so a folder stands for the `.json` files inside it.
The pull request is loaded from either a bare object or a whole event file.
The tests read the reusable workflow as text and assert its inputs, guards and job shapes.
The tests read the caller as text and assert it is thin, passes only declared inputs, and grants no write permission.
The new test runs `review reduce` with a folder and with the same files listed, and asserts the outputs match.
The guide documents the caller shape, the five inputs, the secrets model and what is stable.

flows.title: One review run, from caller to posted review
flows.summary: A pull request event reaches the caller, which hands the pinned commit to the reusable workflow. The build job compiles that osf and finds the work item; each reviewer job runs it with its own key; the last job collects the saved answers and posts.

messages.label: pull_request_target event
messages.note: GitHub reads the caller from the default branch, so a pull request cannot change it.

messages.label: refuse osf-ref != job.workflow_sha
messages.note: A moving reference, or any commit but the workflow's own, fails the job before anything is built.

messages.label: cargo build --release --bin osf
messages.note: The pinned checkout is mounted read-only at /osf-src; the build writes only to build-out.

messages.label: osf review run --reviewer <name> --if-enabled
messages.note: Each job holds only its own provider key and mounts base and pr read-only.

messages.label: review-run-<name> artifact
messages.note: Uploaded with if: always(), so a failed reviewer still contributes a could-not-run.

messages.label: osf review reduce /out/runs
messages.note: The folder is expanded to the .json files inside it, sorted by name.

messages.label: check run and review
messages.note: The last job alone mints the verifier app's token.
